turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Thank you. Um, well, I came in because ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, I've just been having a hard time. I keep getting really wound up over things like invoices and client messages. Then I end up just avoiding them entirely until I'm sitting there crying at my kitchen table, or I realize I'm forgetting normal stuff, like paying my own bills.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient describes developing emotional and behavioral difficulties (getting wound up, avoidance, crying, and functional disruption) directly in response to the stressor of launching a freelance art business.

turns.doctor_question: When you're not dealing with work-related things like invoices or client messages, do you still feel anxious or worried most of the time, or does it mainly happen when you're facing those specific business tasks?
turns.patient_response: Um, no, I don't really feel anxious most of the time. It's pretty much just when I have to deal with the business side of things. Like, if I'm actually just making the art or doing stuff around the house, I feel fine. It really only hits me when I have to look at those specific tasks.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies feeling anxious most of the time, stating that anxiety is limited to specific business tasks rather than occurring persistently across multiple activities.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about these business tasks like invoices or client messages, what specifically worries you the most? Are you worried about how the client might judge your work or message, or is it more about the task itself feeling overwhelming?
turns.patient_response: Um, I don't really know. I haven't thought about it like that. I guess I'm not really sure if it's about them judging me or if it's just the tasks themselves. I just know that when I look at the emails or the spreadsheets, I just feel this wall go up, and I can't seem to get past it.

turns.doctor_question: Besides the business tasks, are there other areas of your life—like social situations, health concerns, or finances in general—where you find yourself feeling anxious or worried regularly?
turns.patient_response: Um, no, not really. I don't really worry about my health or social situations or anything like that. Like I said, I usually feel totally fine. I mean, I guess my own personal bills stress me out a little when I realize I forgot to pay them because I was avoiding my work emails, but in general, no. I've never really been an anxious person about other stuff. It's really just tied to trying to run this art business.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies having regular anxiety or worry across multiple areas of life, stating they do not worry about health or social situations and that their anxiety is solely tied to running their art business.

turns.doctor_question: When you're not actively avoiding these business tasks—like, say, you're just thinking about them or you know you need to do them soon—do you find yourself worrying about them throughout the day, or does the anxiety mainly kick in when you actually sit down and look at the emails or spreadsheets?
turns.patient_response: I think it's mostly when I actually sit down to do them. If I'm busy with my art or doing things around the house, I'm not really thinking about it. I mean, it might pop into my head that I need to send an invoice or reply to someone, but I don't spend the whole day worrying about it. The bad feeling really just kicks in when I open the laptop and actually see the emails or the spreadsheets right in front of me.

turns.doctor_question: When you're away from your laptop or not looking at these business emails and spreadsheets—like, say, you're at dinner or in bed at night—do you find yourself worrying or thinking about them, or does the worry pretty much stop once you're not looking at them?
turns.patient_response: Um, no, not really. Like I said, once I'm away from it, I'm usually fine. I don't lay in bed stressing about the emails or anything. It's really just when I'm sitting there looking at the screen that it gets to me. When I'm doing other things, I'm just focused on whatever I'm doing.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about those business tasks like invoices or emails, do you ever get stuck with the same worrying thoughts repeating over and over in your head that you can't seem to get rid of, or is it more that you just feel dread and want to avoid looking at them?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really get stuck on repeating thoughts like that. It's definitely more of just a feeling of dread. Like, I just really don't want to deal with it, so I put it off and avoid it. But I wouldn't say I have thoughts spinning in my head that I can't turn off.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly denies having recurring, spinning, or unstoppable thoughts when asked about persistent repeating thoughts.

turns.doctor_question: If you had to do these business tasks—like opening the emails or filling out invoices—but you knew for certain that nothing bad would happen and there would be no consequences at all, do you think you'd still feel that same dread and urge to avoid them?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure. I guess... if I knew for a fact that nothing bad would happen, maybe it wouldn't be as bad? But honestly, I just hate doing them so much. It's hard to imagine doing them without feeling that dread, just because they're so overwhelming to me. So I don't know, I'd probably still want to avoid them.

turns.doctor_question: When you're looking at those business emails or invoices, is the main thing that bothers you the fear that the client might judge you or think badly of you, or is it more just that the task itself feels really overwhelming and hard to do?
turns.patient_response: I don't think it's about them judging me. I'm not really worried about what the clients think of me, honestly. It's... it's just the tasks themselves. They just feel really overwhelming and just hard to get through. So yeah, it's definitely just the work itself being too much, not really a fear of the people.

turns.doctor_question: Let me ask this a different way: If you were sitting at your laptop but your business emails and spreadsheets were completely hidden or closed—like, you knew they were there but you couldn't see them—would you still feel that dread and anxiety, or does the anxiety really only happen when you actually see them on the screen?
turns.patient_response: I think... I think if they were closed and I couldn't see them, I wouldn't feel it as much right in that moment. It's really when I open the laptop and actually look at the screen, and see the emails sitting there or the spreadsheet open, that the dread really hits me. If they're out of sight, I know they're still there, but the anxiety isn't as intense until I actually have to look at them.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned the anxiety really kicks in when you see the emails and spreadsheets on your screen. I guess maybe it would still feel overwhelming because it's the same work, but I don't know for a fact since I haven't done it any other way.

turns.doctor_question: When you're not at your laptop—like, if you're away from home for a few hours—does the thought of those business tasks pop into your head and make you feel anxious or stressed, or does the anxiety really only start when you're actually sitting down and can see the emails on your screen?
turns.patient_response: No, it doesn't really pop into my head when I'm away from it. If I'm out doing something else, I'm usually just focused on whatever I'm doing. The anxiety really only starts when I'm back home, sitting down, and I actually open the laptop and see the emails right there in front of me.

turns.doctor_question: When you see those emails or spreadsheets on your laptop screen, does the anxiety feel like a sudden fear or panic reaction to actually looking at them, or does it feel more like a sense of being overwhelmed by how much work needs to be done?
turns.patient_response: It feels more like... just being completely overwhelmed by all the work. It's not like a sudden panic attack or anything like that. I just see it all sitting there and it's like a heavy weight, just dreading having to actually do it all.
